campaign_name: AT-OPT-03 Primary Narration Context Attribution and Compression Feasibility
purpose: Explain why legitimate primary narration requests exceed 20,000 input tokens and identify one safe, measurable compression experiment. Do not change production prompts.
executive_summary: Verdict A/PASS. Live provider calls: 0. The captured F3 prompt was not stored. A rebuild from the pre-continuation snapshot is 83,040 bytes and an admission estimate of 27,744, against a recorded 22,777 input tokens. The 4,967-token gap is unattributed. The user JSON is mostly response_policy (21,638 bytes), instructions (12,596), and turn_packet (10,642). Recent log is 306 bytes. Eleven historical gm.call_gpt requests exceed 20,000 input tokens: five openings at 25,294, plus mid-scene primary and retry calls. Expression calls stay near 100-350. Twelve JSON-equal turn-packet policy keys survive because three siblings differ. Dropping only the equal keys saves 2,637 bytes on the reconstruction, admission estimate minus 879. That is the unstarted AT-OPT-04 experiment. Do not bypass the compact-instruction gate. Do not cap production openings at 3,000. Do not open PR-PLAY-80.

missing_concepts: A stored copy of the provider payload, or a section-size log written at dispatch without storing prompt text.
A live tokenizer count for the equal-key deletion.
does_not_prove: It does not prove a provider-billed token saving.
It does not prove that narration quality survives the equal-key deletion. No live narration was generated.
It does not prove the compact instruction list can be forced while transition_required is true.
It does not prove a Gameplay Benchmark result. No benchmark was run.
The 11 passed tests were not written for the mixed-key change. They do not cover it.
recommended_next_step: Stop. Do not start AT-OPT-04. The proposed experiment is a mixed-key drop inside omit_duplicate_turn_packet_policy, with the equal values left on response_policy. Do not open PR-PLAY-80. Do not cap production openings at 3,000.
